question.problem:
What is the remainder of $-2{x}^{3}-8$ divided by $-{x}^{2}+2x-3?$

The remainder is
{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the dividend is missing the ${x}^{2}$ and $x$ terms. So, we first rewrite it by including the missing terms with zero coefficients, as follows:

$$
-2{x}^{3}-8=-2{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x-8
$$

Now, using the method of polynomial division, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,\,\,\,2x+4 \\  & -{x}^{2}+2x-3\,\enclose{longdiv}{\,\,-2{x}^{3}+0{x}^{2}+0x-\phantom{0}8\,\,} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,{-2{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-6x}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,-4{x}^{2}+6x-8 \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,{-4{x}^{2}+8x-12}_{―} \\  & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,-\,2x+4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

- the quotient is $2x+4,$ and

- the remainder is $-2x+4.$
